title: Polarization-Controlled Structural Modulation in the Single Atomic Layer at the PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3/LaNiO3 Interface
content: The development of all-oxide field-effect devices has garnered significant interest for next-generation electronic applications, particularly in non-volatile memory and energy-efficient computing. Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) leveraging perovskite oxide heterostructures enable non-volatile data storage via ferroelectric polarization switching, which modulates carrier density in the channel material. In previous work, FeFETs incorporating a Pb(Zr,Ti)O3 (PZT) ferroelectric gate and an ultrathin LaNiO3 (LNO) conductive channel on a SrTiO3 (STO) substrate exhibited a remarkable conductivity change (∼1 order of magnitude) at room temperature [1]. However, the underlying mechanisms governing this anomalous conduction modulation remain unresolved.
